core_image: 孩子望着餐桌上的面包，肚子咕咕作响
scene: 长跑结束后，孩子们都饿了。After the long run, the children were hungry.

senses.title: Needing food

senses.example: After the long run, the children were hungry.

intro.en: Hungry is the adjective built on the old word hunger.

definition_en: to chase animals for food or sport, or to search for something
core_image: 猎人弯腰查看雪地上的脚印
scene: 猎人在森林里寻找鹿的踪迹。The hunter hunted for deer tracks in the forest.
sceneCN: 这里 hunt 是「打猎；寻找」（第 1 个义项）；句意：猎人在森林里寻找鹿的踪迹。

senses.title: To chase animals
senses.definition: to chase and kill animals for food or sport
senses.definitionCN: 为食物或娱乐追捕并杀死动物
senses.example: The hunter hunted for deer tracks in the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 猎人在森林里寻找鹿的踪迹。
senses.why: This is the old sense of the chase.
senses.whyCN: 这是古老的追猎义项。

senses.title: To search carefully
senses.definition: to look for something with effort
senses.example: We hunted for the missing keys.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到处寻找丢失的钥匙。
senses.why: The chase becomes a search for objects.
senses.whyCN: 追猎变成对物品的搜寻。

senses.title: To pursue someone
senses.definition: to chase someone in order to catch them
senses.example: The police hunted the escaped prisoner.
senses.exampleCN: 警方追捕逃跑的囚犯。
senses.why: Here the object is a person rather than an animal.
senses.whyCN: 这里对象是人而非动物。

intro.en: Hunt is an old Germanic word for chasing game.
intro.cn: hunt 是表示追猎猎物的古老日耳曼词。

note.en: Hunt is compared with look-alike words and with words for chasing.

definition_en: to move or act quickly, or to make someone do so
core_image: 街角的人加快脚步，手里提着晃动的包
scene: 她匆匆赶去车站。She hurried to the station.
sceneCN: 这里 hurry 是「赶快」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她匆匆赶去车站。

senses.title: To move quickly
senses.definition: to move or act with speed
senses.example: She hurried to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她匆匆赶去车站。
senses.why: This is the core sense of acting fast.
senses.whyCN: 这是快速行动的核心义项。

senses.title: To make someone move faster
senses.definition: to make someone do something more quickly
senses.example: The teacher hurried the students along.
senses.exampleCN: 老师催促学生们快点走。
senses.why: Here the verb acts on another person.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词作用于他人。

senses.title: A state of rushing
senses.definition: the state of needing to move fast
senses.example: There is no hurry, so take your time.
senses.exampleCN: 不着急，慢慢来。
senses.why: As a noun it names the pressure of speed.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时指速度带来的压力。

intro.en: Hurry appeared in English with an uncertain origin, probably imitating rushed movement.
intro.cn: hurry 出现在英语中时来源不明，可能模仿匆忙的动作。

items.en: The word appears without a clear older source.
items.cn: 这个词没有清楚的更早来源。

items.en: Hurry meant to move with haste.

definition_en: to cause pain or injury, or to feel pain
core_image: 孩子捂着撞到桌角的膝盖，眼里含着泪
scene: 他摔伤了膝盖。He hurt his knee when he fell.
sceneCN: 这里 hurt 是「使受伤」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他摔伤了膝盖。

senses.title: To cause physical pain
senses.definition: to cause pain or injury to a body
senses.example: He hurt his knee when he fell.
senses.exampleCN: 他摔伤了膝盖。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的身体义项。

senses.title: To feel pain
senses.definition: to feel pain in the body
senses.example: My feet hurt after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 走了很久之后我的脚很疼。
senses.why: Here the subject is the person or body part in pain.
senses.whyCN: 这里主语是感到疼痛的人或部位。

senses.title: To wound feelings
senses.definition: to make someone feel unhappy or upset
senses.example: His words hurt her deeply.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话深深伤害了她。
senses.why: The bodily sense extends to emotional pain.
senses.whyCN: 身体义延伸到情感痛苦。

intro.en: Hurt came from a French verb meaning to strike or knock.
intro.cn: hurt 来自一个意为「击打、撞击」的法语动词。

normal.cn: 她今天生病了，留在家里。

normal.en: He fell ill during the trip.
normal.cn: 他在旅途中病倒了。

normal.en: Ill news travelled fast.
normal.cn: 坏消息传得很快。

normal.en: The plan boded ill for the project.
normal.cn: 这个计划对项目不利。

normal.en: He felt ill at ease in the crowd.
normal.cn: 他在人群中感到不自在。

abstract.en: Ill links the sick body with the bad event.
abstract.cn: ill 把生病的身体与坏事件连在一起。

abstract.en: What is ill is out of its proper order.
abstract.cn: 生病之物失去了本来的秩序。

abstract.en: Health and fortune can both turn ill.
abstract.cn: 健康与运气都可能变坏。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 古诺斯语 illr（坏的）
dict_mnemonic.text: ill 来自古诺斯语 illr，本指坏的、恶的，后来主要用于健康，表示生病，也可表示有害或不利。

root: 来自古诺斯语 illr（坏的、恶的），词义后来转向健康与不利。

sensesIntro.en: Ill means not healthy, bad or harmful, or in an unfavourable way.
sensesIntro.cn: ill 表示生病、有害或不利。

core.en: A body or an event out of its proper order.
core.cn: 身体或事件失去了应有的秩序。

branches.en: She was ill today and stayed home.
branches.cn: 她今天生病了，留在家里。

branches.en: He fell ill during the trip.
branches.cn: 他在旅途中病倒了。

branches.en: Ill news travelled fast.
branches.cn: 坏消息传得很快。

branches.en: The plan boded ill for the project.
branches.cn: 这个计划对项目不利。

branches.en: Bad news and poor health share the word ill.
branches.cn: 坏消息与健康不佳共用 ill。

intro.en: Ill forms illness and the comparative worse and worst.
intro.cn: ill 构成 illness，并有比较级 worse 与最高级 worst。

latinIntro.en: Ill is Norse; Latin malus, bad, plays a similar role in other words.
latinIntro.cn: ill 属诺斯语；拉丁语 malus（坏的）在其他词中起类似作用。
